title: Lab notes: regenerating fungal-derived adsorption membranes after PFAS capture

aims.summary: Regenerate fungal-derived adsorption membranes after PFAS capture without the solvent waste of methanol washing.
Degrade captured PFAS directly on the membrane with a visible-light photocatalyst that does not damage the fungal matrix.

findings.summary: Fungal-derived membranes captured more than 90 % of PFOA from spiked tap water in batch tests.
Methanol regeneration recovered only 60 % of the capacity after three cycles.

methods.name: Batch adsorption tests
methods.detail: PFOA-spiked tap water at 1 µg L-1.

open_questions.summary: Which visible-light photocatalyst degrades captured PFAS without damaging the fungal matrix?
Is the membrane thermally stable up to 80 °C?
Which partners with visible-LED photocatalysis experience for persistent organic pollutants could join?
